title: Alcohol-fuelled rampage leads to five-month sentence
subtitle: SUMMERSIDE - A 22-year-old city man was sentenced for several offences after a drunken rampage on the streets of Summerside.
article: Matthew John Rice pleaded guilty Tuesday in provincial court to single counts of break-and-enter, indecent exposure, assault and theft.

At around 8 p.m. on Aug. 10, police received a report of an intoxicated, shirtless man walking down Granville Street and attempting to kick and punch passing vehicles. Officers found Rice on Lefurgey Avenue arguing with another man, clearly intoxicated, and arrested him for being drunk in public.
Shortly after his arrest, police discovered Rice had attempted to enter several homes along Lefurgey Avenue.

At one address, he forced himself inside the front door of a senior woman's residence after asking to use her phone. As the victim yelled for Rice to leave, he pushed her and threw a chair across the room before leaving the home.
At another residence on Lefurgey, Rice again tried to force his way into the home of a woman. As she attempted to lock the door, he grabbed the victim's left arm.
The woman screamed and Rice fled, however the victim's arm was left sore and swollen from the assault.

The witness who initially called the police said he first came into contact with Rice when he noticed him standing outside the window of his basement apartment. The witness said Rice pulled down his pants and exposed himself before urinating on a tree.
Another witness, a woman and her son on Granville Street, also saw Rice walking through traffic and urinating in full view of passers-by.

In an unrelated matter, Rice was also arrested on Aug. 29 for stealing a 1.75-litre bottle of rum from the Waterfront liquor store. Staff members chased Rice from the store, but were unable to catch him.
He was later arrested for being drunk in public, and police identified him from security footage from the liquor store.
Rice has a prior record for a break-and-enter and theft in 2010 and an assault in 2011, but received a suspended sentence on each occasion.
Defence attorney Trish Cheverie said her client has little recollection of the Aug. 10 events because of his intoxication, and was "shocked" when police detailed what he'd done.

Judge Jeff Lantz sentenced Rice to four months in jail for the break-and-enter, and a combined 31 days for the remaining offences. He will be on probation for two years and must undergo assessment, counseling and treatment for any addictions or mental health issues.
